content.title: USA wins epic vs Dominican Republic to reach World Baseball Classic title game: Highlights
content.text: March 15, 2026Updated March 16, 2026, 2:33 a.m. ETMIAMI — It was an instant classic, one that will be shown for years on MLB Network re-runs, but instead of a historic power display, it was the pitching Sunday night that will be remembered in this World Baseball Classic epic.USA’s power arms, from Paul Skenes to Mason Miller, dominated the Dominican Republic’s vaunted lineup, and the Americans advanced to the WBC championship game with a 2-1 win in front of a sellout crowd of 36,337 at loanDepot Park.The Dominican Republic, which was averaging more than 10 runs a game, simply looked overmatched at the plate.The DR's lone run was on Junior Caminero’s two-out homer in the second inning.Oh, they had their chances, producing eight hits, but time after time, they failed to get the clutch hit they needed. The game ended with closer Miller retiring Geraldo Perdomo to leave Julio Rodriguez stranded on third base.And just like, USA is back in the championship game Tuesday night, and will play the winner of Monday's Venezuela-Italy semiinal.“This is what you dream about as a kid," Aaron Judge said, “playing with the best of the best. We've got the best squad out there. They've got the best squad out there. It's what you play when you're in your backyard playing Wiffle Ball. It’s moments like this you dream about."Who would ever have imagined that USA would hit two homers in a span of three batters in the fourth inning from Gunnar Henderson and Roman Anthony, produce just one hit the rest of the night, and still win?“If we play our game," USA shortstop Bobby Witt said before the game, “I feel like we can beat any team in the world."Whether it was a boring brand of baseball or not, the Americans proved once again that powerful pitching can shut down the mightiest offense in the land.“It's funny to think about the American way of baseball and the Dominican way of baseball and all this kind of stuff,’’ USA first baseman Bryce Harper said, “but it's awesome to see all these cultures come together from Asia to Latin countries to America."That's what's so great about our game."Japan plays a certain game. America plays a certain game. Latin American countries play a certain game. We're all in this tournament feeding off of playing a great game, and that's what makes our game so great is there's so many different cultures that play this game.“I can't dance a lick like [Fernando] Tatis can, but I have fun playing this game."The game was a clash of stars, featuring players who won 12 MVP awards, selected to more than 50 All-Star games, and 18 players who received top-10 MVP votes last season.Yet, it was the powerful USA arms that stole the show, with Judge and Dominican Republic center fielder Julio Rodriguez trading highlight defensive plays.It was a game that will be etched in every player’s memory.There was an electric atmosphere simply during batting practice, but Dominican DH Junior Caminero amped up the crowd in the second inning swatting an 84-mph sweeper 401-foot homer over the left-field fence, sending the sellout crowd dancing in the aisles and Caminero pounding his chest as he sailed around the bases.It was the only real mistake Skenes made all night, but he got out of trouble in the third and fourth innings.In the third, Ketel Marte hit a sharp two-out single to Judge, advancing Fernando Tatis Jr. to second base, but foolishly, he decided to test Judge’s arm. Silly mistake. Judge made a perfect throw, easily nailing Tatis, while Juan Soto stood on the on-deck circle looking in disbelief.The Dominican Republic loaded the bases with two outs in the fourth inning, but Skenes held firm to get a lazy fly-out by No. 8 hitter Austin Wells.Buy World Baseball Classic tickets!Luis Severino, who was throwing 98 mph – 3 mph faster than normal – wiggled his way out of his own trouble in his 3 ⅓-inning outing, but twice escaped jams.In the third inning, he gave up a one-out single to Witt and a double to Harper, and with Judge coming to the plate. Even with first base open, Dominican manager Albert Pujols opted to have Severino pitch to Judge. He struck him out on five pitches. Next up, left-handed slugger Kyle Schwarber. He took a called third strike on a sweeper across the plate.Severino pounded his chest and stomped off the mound as the crowd went wild.But leading off the top of the fourth, Gunnar Henderson hit Severino's 95-mph cutter, 400 feet over the right-field wall.Severino was yanked after giving up a hard line drive out to Will Smith, and 21-year-old left-handed hitter Roman Anthony greeted lefty reliever Gregory Soto with a 421-foot shot over the center-field wall, giving USA a 2-1 lead.“Roman’s a class act," Judge said. “Just to be 21 years old, and to be doing what he's doing on the biggest stage in baseball every single night. We see him in the cage. He's watching Bryce [Harper]. He's asking questions.“I think that's such a cool thing to see, at such a young age to ask questions, to be observant like that, and just trying to get better. So, the Red Sox definitely have a good one in him."Now, this team will come together one more time, trying to win its second WBC title – after losing in the 2023 title game to Japan.“Each guy checked their ego at the door and stepped in here and threw on the USA [jersey]," Judge said, “and they're representing their country the right way. So it's been an absolute blast."– Bob NightengaleHere's how the game unfolded: To the ninth: USA 2, Dominican Republic 1Garrett Whitlock retired the heart of the Dominican Republic lineup in order in the eighth inning to send this game to the ninth inning with Team USA still leading 2-1. David Bednar locks in to keep USA in frontRight-hander David Bednar came in to pitch for the Americans in the bottom of the seventh and the Dominican Republic got runners to second and third with one one out on Austin Wells' double, Geraldo Perdomo's single and stolen base. But Bednar, the New York Yankees' closer, responded by striking out Fernando Tatis Jr. and Ketel Marte swinging to escape unscathed. Tyler Rogers gets huge double playPaul Skenes came out of the game with runners on first and second in the bottom of the fifth, relieved by side-armer Tyler Rogers. The right-hander got Juan Soto to ground into a double play to end the inning and keep Team USA in front 2-1 heading into the sixth.Julio Rodriguez robs Aaron JudgeDominican Republic center fielder Julio Rodriguez made a stunning catch to rob Aaron Judge of a home run in the fifth inning of the World Baseball Classic semifinal.Judge, the New York Yankees' three-time MVP and captain of Team USA, drove a pitch from Juan Mejia to center at loanDepot Park in Miami and Rodriguez timed his leap perfectly at the wall to make the play.An All-Star three times in four MLB seasons with the Seattle Mariners, Rodriguez popped up to celebrate and immediately while Judge could only smile after being robbed of extra bases.The Americans lead 2-1 heading into the bottom of the fifth. Paul Skenes gets out of bases-loaded jamThe Dominican Republic loaded the bases against Paul Skenes in the bottom of the fourth, starting with Vladimir Guerrero Jr.'s double. Manny Machado singled and then Skenes hit Julio Rodriguez with two outs, bringing Austin Wells to the plate. On the fifth pitch of the at-bat, Skenes got Wells to fly out to left field and strand all three runners. Roman Anthony home run puts USA in frontGregory Soto came into the game for the left-on-left matchup with Roman Anthony, but the Boston Red Sox phenom smashed a go-ahead solo home run to center field, giving Team USA a 2-1 advantage. Gunnar Henderson home run ties it upInserted into the lineup due to his unbelievable numbers against DR starter Luis Severino (7-for-9 career), Gunnar Henderson led off the top of the fourth with a solo home run to right-center, tying this WBC semifinal 1-1.Severino got the next batter and then Dominican Republic manager Albert Pujols made a pitching change, bringing in lefty Gregory Soto to face Roman Anthony with one out. Aaron Judge guns down Tatis to end thirdFernando Tatis Jr. tried to go first-to-third on Ketel Marte's single into right field with top outs in the bottom of the third, but Aaron Judge delivered a perfect throw to get Tatis at third and end the inning. It was the second time in the 2026 WBC that Judge has caught a runner at third base from right field. Luis Severino escapes: DR 1, USA 0 in thirdIn the top of the third, Bobby Witt Jr.'s single and Bryce Harper's double gave Team USA runners on second and third with one out. But Luis Severino dug deep to strike out Aaron Judge and Kyle Schwarber and get out of the inning. Junior Caminero home run puts DR in frontWith two outs in the bottom of the second, Tampa Bay Rays slugger Junior Camerino clubbed a Paul Skenes offering over the left field wall to open the scoring in Miami. Camerino launched his bat and teammates poured out of the dugout to celebrate.Caminero, 22, hit 45 home runs with 110 RBIs for the Tampa Bay Rays in 2025, finishing ninth in AL MVP. Paul Skenes makes quick work of DR in firstPaul Skenes needed just nine pitches to get through the first inning, getting Fernando Tatis Jr. to fly out to left and Ketel Marte to pop out to second before Brice Turang made a sliding play to rob Juan Soto of a hit and end the bottom of the first. Luis Severino squashes two-out rallyLuis Severino struck out Bobby Witt Jr. and Bryce Harper to start the game and had Aaron Judge in a 1-2 count but ultimately gave up a single to the three-time MVP. Severino hit Kyle Schwarber to move to Judge to second, but Gunnar Henderson grounded out to second to end the threat.USA starting lineup tonight vs DRStarting pitcher: RHP Paul SkenesBobby Witt Jr. – expressing their desire to play in the 2028 Olympics, and it’s possible that the players union could reach a deal with MLB permitting players to participate, independent of a new collective bargaining agreement.Bruce Meyer, executive director of the players association, fully believes that MLB will impose a lockout when the current CBA expires on Dec. 1, but said Sunday that a deal could be reached before Dec. 1 permitting MLB players to be play in the Olympics - in Los Angeles – for the first time.Then again, everything changes if the lockout wipes out the entire 2027 season.– Bob You have a country that saw you grow and become who you are these days,” Juan Soto told reporters before Sunday’s game. “You cannot be more proud to give them back a little bit of what they've been giving you all these years.“I think it's the way everybody feels playing in the WBC.
